title: Interface Basics
definition: An interface is a syntax in TypeScript used to define the shape of an object. It explicitly names a specific combination of properties and their types.
simpleExplanation: An interface is a contract. If a component says 'I need a User object', the Interface is the document that lists exactly what makes an object a 'User'. If your object doesn't match the contract (e.g., missing an email), it gets rejected.
realWorldExample: Defining the props for a React component: `interface ButtonProps { label: string; onClick: () => void; }`.

basic: Can an interface define a function type?
intermediate: Can you add properties to an interface after it is defined?
advanced: What is the difference between an Interface and a Type Alias?

answers.question: Can an interface define a function type?
answers.answer: Yes. While usually used for objects, you can use an interface to define a function signature using an anonymous method signature: `interface MathFunc { (a: number, b: number): number }`.

answers.question: Can you add properties to an interface later?
answers.answer: Yes! This is called 'Declaration Merging'. If you declare `interface User { name: string }` and later in the same file declare `interface User { age: number }`, TS merges them into one single interface containing both properties.
